alignments.note: Rule 102: the article's complement is a substantival numeral with no expressed head noun, so the supplied determiner and the supplied nominal day are both the article's and the unit heads on day; the dative's on rides along under rule 21, and the phrase is discontinuous under rule 15 exactly as τὸν πτωχόν → the … man is. Rule 17's on the → the clause does not reach this, because a nominal competes; rule 17's generic-noun clause is scoped to anarthrous Greek under rule 102.
Rule 102: with a Greek article standing to take the determiner and the supplied noun, the numeral is left bare.
Rule 21: of the on the article.
Genitive of time; rule 21's determinerless clause keeps the supplied at with the noun, discontinuously under rule 15.
Rule 9: head on the lexical verb.
Rule 51: Greek anarthrous, so the supplied determiner is a rule 7 helper on the noun.
Rule 9: subject and auxiliary ride with the verb, head on prepared.

review_notes: Corrected s001/s003: the accepted alignment gave on the to the article headed on the and first day to μιᾷ headed on first, which is rule 17's generic-noun clause. Rule 102 scopes that clause to anarthrous Greek and is unanimous the other way where a Greek article stands to take the determiner, so the article takes on the … day headed on day and the numeral keeps a bare first.
s006 ὄρθρου takes the supplied at because no Greek preposition is expressed and rule 21 forbids leaving it on an article the ASV gave no determiner.
LUK.24.7 and LUK.24.46 are not parallels for the corrected unit: there the noun ἡμέρᾳ is expressed, so the article takes only the.
